title: Comparative Government — Liberty vs. Tyranny
description: Test your understanding of different governmental systems and the Biblical principles that distinguish liberty from tyranny.

questions.question: According to the Declaration of Independence, where do human rights come from?
options: From the government
From the Creator
From the Constitution
From the social contract
questions.explanation: The Declaration states that people 'are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights,' establishing that rights come from God, not from any human authority.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a constitutional republic and a pure democracy?
options: A republic has no elections
A pure democracy gives every citizen a government job
A constitutional republic limits government power through a written constitution
A pure democracy is always larger than a republic
questions.explanation: In a constitutional republic, a written constitution limits government power and protects individual rights, even against majority will. Pure democracy has no such limits.

questions.question: What was Karl Marx's view of religion?
options: It was the foundation of a just society
It was neutral and unimportant
It was 'the opium of the people' — a tool to pacify the masses
It should be the basis for communist government
questions.explanation: Marx viewed religion as a tool used to keep oppressed people content with their suffering, and communist ideology requires the elimination of religion because it points to an authority above the state.

questions.question: Which verse from Isaiah inspired the American separation of powers into three branches?
options: Isaiah 9:6
Isaiah 33:22 — 'The LORD is our judge, lawgiver, and king'
Isaiah 40:31
Isaiah 53:5
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:22 identifies three functions of governance — judicial, legislative, and executive — united only in God. The Founders separated these functions because they believed only God could be trusted with all three.

questions.question: What was Mussolini's definition of totalitarianism?
options: Government by the military alone
Everything within the state, nothing outside the state, nothing against the state
A government elected by all citizens
A government that controls only the economy
questions.explanation: Mussolini's motto captures the essence of totalitarianism: the state claims authority over every aspect of human life, leaving no sphere — family, church, individual conscience — free from government control.

questions.question: What did Alexis de Tocqueville warn about regarding American democracy?
options: That America would become a monarchy
That the tyranny of the majority could oppress minorities
That democracy would collapse within a century
That Americans were too religious for democracy to work
questions.explanation: Tocqueville identified the 'tyranny of the majority' as a significant danger in democratic societies — the possibility that the majority could use its power to suppress the rights of minorities and dissenters.

questions.question: Who delivered the 'City upon a Hill' sermon that shaped American exceptionalism?
options: George Washington
Benjamin Franklin
John Winthrop
Jonathan Edwards
questions.explanation: John Winthrop delivered 'A Model of Christian Charity' aboard the Arbella in 1630, declaring the Massachusetts Bay Colony a 'city upon a hill' — a model of Christian community accountable to God.

questions.question: What do fascism and communism have in common despite their surface differences?
options: Both support free markets and individual liberty
Both are totalitarian systems that reject God and suppress individual rights
Both originated in ancient Greece
Both limit government power through constitutions
questions.explanation: Despite differing in economic theory and national vs. international focus, both fascism and communism are totalitarian, reject Biblical authority, suppress individual rights, and concentrate power in a ruling elite.

questions.question: Why did John Adams say the Constitution was made 'only for a moral and religious people'?
options: Because only religious people can read
Because the Constitution requires church membership
Because free government depends on citizens who govern themselves according to moral principles
Because the Constitution was written in a church
questions.explanation: Adams understood that a system of limited government with maximum individual liberty can only work if citizens voluntarily restrain themselves according to moral principles — and he believed true morality comes from religious faith.

questions.question: According to the 'higher law' tradition, what happens when a human law contradicts God's moral law?
options: The human law must always be obeyed
The human law is 'no law at all' and Christians may be obligated to resist it
God's law becomes void
Both laws are equally valid
questions.explanation: Thomas Aquinas taught that human law must conform to God's natural and eternal law. When it does not, it is a corruption of law, and Christians have both the right and duty to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29).
